about: The 1989 village shop counter that replaces the vanilla yellow market cart CounterShop_01 behind every till: a dark-stained oak carcass with varnished tongue-and-groove (lambris) panels on the customer front and sides, a black kick plinth, a brown laminate worktop with an aluminium edge, open shelves on the staff side with kraft paper bags and a wrapping-paper roll. ShopCounterTill adds an early-electronic cash register (cream plastic, sloped keyboard and cash drawer toward the clerk, a green figure display on a post toward the customer, a receipt roll) and a rubber change mat on the customer half. Built by build.py in headless Blender from boxes and procedural textures: no base-game mesh reads as a shop counter with a till, and Meshy is reserved for fish and masks. Core asset: no text, no brand, no place name.

layout_m.about: Enfusion metres, x right, y up, z forward. The footprint is the vanilla CounterShop_01 it replaces (x -0.75..0.75, y 0..1.039, z -0.525..0.597, same origin), so every placed counter keeps its seat and everything standing on it keeps its height. The customer front is +z; the clerk stands on the -z side (Saint-Philippe bakery clerk 0.98 m behind the origin).

emissive.about: The till's figure display glows faintly green.
